title: Topics Codebook
subtitle: Illinois Policy Agendas Project
contact: Dr. E.J. Fagan, Project Director, ejfagan at uic.edu
citation: Fagan, E.J. and Annika Ness. 2025. Illinois Agendas Project: Codebook.
intro: Observations in Illinois Policy Agendas datasets are coded according to the guidelines and topic system maintained by the Comparative Agendas Project. This codebook is adapted from the original codebook created by Baumgartner and Jones. It follows the rules and examples of the U.S. codebook, which can be found at www.comparativeagendas.com/us.

Each entry is coded into one of 20 major topics and 220 subtopics. In this codebook, we provide a series of general coding guidelines for classifying observations, a complete list of all major topics and subtopics, and examples of cases coded in each subtopic. Users should note that not all topic and subtopic numbers are consecutive, and that the coding system is hierarchal: each subtopic falls within a single major topic. Analysts concerned with identifying each case dealing with a particular issue may want to use care in also examining the textual summaries for cases in related subtopics and in the ‘general’ subtopic, since these can include cases that discuss multiple subtopics.

The CAP codebook was originally developed to classify federal U.S. policymaking, particularly in Congress, beginning in 1945. As a result, many subtopics have little relevance to state government and contain few, if any, Illinois observations.

The Comparative Agendas Project trains human coders on previous versions of the dataset until they agree with previous coders at approximately 95% on the major topic level and 75% on the subtopic level. For most datasets, each observation is coded by two independent humans. Where the coders disagree, the coders debate the appropriate code. If no consensus is reached, a third coder breaks the tie.

To reduce coding costs, some datasets are first run through the CAP Babel Machine’s supervised machine learning model. This model is specifically tuned to code CAP data using hundreds of thousands of hand-coded observations as training data. Babel generates a predicted probability for each subtopic area. Any observations with a predicted probability for one code over 0.95 are automatically coded—44% of observations. All others are coded by humans.

We plan to add more datasets going forward, such as Illinois media, think tank reports and executive orders.
datasets: State of the State Speeches by Illinois Governors (2005-present)
Substantive bills introduced into the Illinois General Assembly (2025-present)
Bills are only coded for subtopic by human coders from 2025-present. We are also working on a dataset of prior bills but only coded for the major topic using the CAP Babel Machine model.
guidelines: Observations are coded according to the single predominant, substantive policy area rather than the targets of particular policies or the policy instrument utilized.

Observations that discuss appropriations for particular departments and agencies are coded according to their substantive policy area. Those that discuss appropriations for multiple departments and agencies that span multiple major topic codes are coded as general government operations (code 2000). Budgets and general discussions of budgets should be coded as 105.
The “general” (NN00) subtopic includes cases where more than one distinct subtopic was discussed within a single major topic area.
While it is uncommon that observations not related to appropriations equally span two major topic areas, these observations are assigned the numerically lower major or subtopic code.

subs.name: Tax Policy
subs.rule: Observations related to general tax policy. Specific tax changes should be coded based upon the subject matter. For instance, deductions for mortgages should go in mortgages; tax incentives to promote child care should go in child care. However, general tax reform packages that include changes to multiple substantive areas should be coded as 107.
subs.see: 2009 IRS administration.

subs.rule: Observations related to general macroeconomic industrial policy. Specific industrial policy changes affecting a substantive policy area (e.g. automobile manufacturing bailouts) should be coded in their substantive area.
subs.see: Specific tax incentives for industries should be coded under their substantive area, such as 1006 for tax breaks to encourage automobile manufacturing. 1806 international business competition; 1400s economic development programs.

subs.see: 601 GI Bill and military academies; 1609 veterans; 1612 reserves.

subs.name: Veteran's Issues
subs.rule: Observations related to veteran policy. Observations related to the provision of services non-specific to veterans but targeted at veterans, such as health care or housing, should be coded in their substantive area. Observations spanning multiple subtopics of such policy areas should be coded as general veteran policy.
subs.see: 300 series for veteran health care; 601 veteran education benefits; 1407 veteran housing; 1409 homeless veterans; 2008 designating/naming Veterans Administration hospitals and medical centers; 1608 on-base military housing and retired military personnel; 502 for job training.

subs.name: Military Procurement
subs.rule: Observations related to defense procurement.
subs.see: 1617 oversight of defense contractors and contractor fraud; 1604 adequacy of supplies.

subs.name: Military Installations
subs.rule: Observations related to military installations and construction.

subs.name: National Guard and Reserves
subs.rule: Observations related to the National Guard and Reserves.
subs.see: 601 ROTC college education.

subs.name: Military Waste Disposal
subs.rule: Observations related to military waste disposal and environmental issues.
subs.see: 704 nonmilitary hazardous waste disposal.

subs.name: Homeland Security
subs.rule: Observations related to civilian efforts to prevent or mitigate threats from foreign or non-state actors against the United States homeland.
subs.see: 200s hate crimes; 1201 border patrol; 1523 FEMA domestic (weather related) disaster relief; 1927 efforts to counter international terrorism not targeted at the United States; 1619 military operations against terrorism.
notes: For issues related to the Department of Homeland Security and domestic terrorism prevention efforts, see the general coding guidelines above.

subs.name: DOD Civilian Issues
subs.rule: Observations related to Department of Defense civilian personnel and military base closings.

subs.name: Military Contractors
subs.rule: Observations related to oversight of defense contracts and contractors.

subs.name: War
subs.rule: Observations related to active military operations and wars and prisoners of war captured by the United States.
subs.see: 1620 settlement of war-related claims against the U.S. Government; 200s civil rights-related policy related to war or prisoners of war.

subs.name: Relief of Claims Against Military
subs.rule: Observations related to the relief of claims against the U.S. military.
subs.see: 1929 International or Foreign Claims Act; Foreign Claims Settlement Commission; 2015 claims against the U.S. Government.

subs.name: Defense (R&D)
subs.rule: Observations related to defense research and development.
subs.see: 1610 procurement.

subs.name: Defense (Other)
subs.see: 2101 military parks and memorials. 17. Space, Science and Communications

subs.name: Science and Communication (General)
subs.rule: Observations combining multiple space, science, technology and communication subtopics, appropriations for related agencies, and general space, science, technology and communications policy.
subs.see: 1798 NSF research funding.

subs.name: Space Exploration
subs.rule: Observations related to public space programs.

subs.name: Commercial Use of Space
subs.rule: Observations related to the private use of space.
subs.see: 1707 satellite TV broadcasting; 1708 weather satellites.

subs.name: Technology Transfer
subs.rule: Observations related to international scientific cooperation and technology transfer.
subs.see: 1803 restrictions on exports of high technology.

subs.name: Telecommunications
subs.rule: Observations related to telephones and the regulation of telecommunication.
subs.see: 208 telephone privacy; 1525 telephone marketing fraud.

subs.name: Broadcast Communications
subs.rule: Observations related to the broadcast media industry, broadband internet, and the electromagnetic spectrum.
subs.see: 1929 Radio Free Europe program.

subs.name: Weather and Oceanography
subs.rule: Observations related to weather forecasting, geological surveys and oceanography.
subs.see: 710 protection of marine environments.

subs.name: Computers and the Internet
subs.rule: Observations relating to computers, and the internet.
subs.see: 1615 cyberterrorism against the United States; 1600s defense-related cybersecurity; 1202 individual prosecutions against cybercriminals.
notes: Issues related to specific issues with the Internet should be coded in their respective categories. For example, financial exploitation over the Internet should go in white collar crime (code 1202).

subs.name: Research and Development
subs.rule: Observations related to general scientific research and development and space, technology and communications research and development.
subs.see: 398 health care science and research; 898 energy science and research.

subs.name: Trade (General)
subs.rule: Observations combining trade subtopics, appropriations for trade agencies, and general trade policy.
subs.see: 401 foreign agricultural trade.

subs.name: Trade Negotiations and Disputes
subs.rule: Observations related to trade negotiations, disputes and agreements.
subs.see: 401 foreign agricultural trade.

subs.name: Exports
subs.rule: Observations related to Illinois exports and export promotion.

subs.name: International Private Investments
subs.rule: Observations related to Illinois international private business investments.

subs.name: Balance and Payments, Competitiveness
subs.rule: Observations related to the international competitiveness of Illinois businesses.
subs.see: 108 domestic industry productivity.

subs.name: Imports and Tariffs
subs.rule: Observations related to U.S. tariffs on imports and non-tariff barriers to trade, and the regulation of imports.

subs.name: Exchange Rates
subs.rule: Observations related to U.S. dollar exchange rates and related foreign exchange rates and the regulation of currency exchanges.

subs.name: International Affairs (General)
subs.rule: Observations combining multiple international affairs subtopics, appropriations for international affairs agencies, and general international affairs policy.

subs.name: Foreign Aid
subs.rule: Observations related to non-military foreign aid provided by the United States.
subs.see: 1606 military aid.

subs.name: International Resources Agreements
subs.rule: Observations related to international agreements related to resources exploitation.

subs.name: Developing Countries Issues
subs.rule: Observations related to problems specific to developing countries other than finance.
subs.see: 1901 foreign aid as a solution to developing country problems; 1906 IMF/World Bank solutions to developing country problems; 1926 UN solutions to developing country problems.

subs.name: International Financial Institutions
subs.rule: Observations related to multilateral international financial institutions and aid agencies and international financial.

subs.name: European Issues
subs.rule: Observations related to Western Europe and the European Union.
notes: See above guideline #5 regarding the coding of observations that mention foreign countries.

subs.name: Panama Canal
subs.rule: Observations related to the Panama Canal.

subs.name: Other/Specific Country Issues
subs.rule: Observations related specifically to non-EU countries and relations with Illinois.
subs.see: 1605 U.S.-Soviet arms agreements; 1901 U.S. foreign aid to the former Soviet Union; 1910 issues dealing with the conflict between Turkey and Greece over Cyprus.

subs.name: Human Rights
subs.rule: Observations related to human rights issues and democracy outside of the United States.

subs.name: International Organizations
subs.rule: Observations related to international organizations other than finance, including Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs).
subs.see: 1602 UN peace-keeping force issues.

subs.name: International Terrorism
subs.rule: Observations related to terrorism that is not directly targeting the U.S.
subs.see: 1003 efforts to prevent hijacking in the U.S.; 1615 Department of Homeland Security-related functions and domestic terrorism prevention efforts within borders; 1619 military actions against terrorism.

subs.name: Diplomacy, Illinois Citizens Abroad
subs.rule: Observations related to U.S. diplomacy, Illinois citizens living abroad, and international travel by Illinois persons.
subs.see: 1603 espionage; 208 display of USIA programs in US.

subs.name: Government Operations (General)
subs.rule: Observations related to combinations of government operations subtopics, omnibus or multiple appropriations bills, appropriations for government operations agencies, and general government operations policy.

subs.name: Intergovernmental Relations
subs.rule: Observations related to the relationship between the state government and local governments.

subs.name: Efficiency and Bureaucratic Oversight
subs.rule: Observations related to efficiency, regulatory policy, and general oversight of the bureaucracy.
subs.see: Appropriations for or oversight of specific departments and agencies see topical field.

subs.name: Postal Service
subs.rule: Observations related to the postal services.
subs.see: 201 racial discrimination in the USPS; 2008 construction or naming of post office buildings.

subs.name: Civil Service Issues
subs.rule: Observations related to civil service issues and government civilian personnel management.
subs.see: 200s discrimination in government employment; 300s state employee health benefits; 503 state/local public sector pensions; 2003 postal employees; 2012 political activities of state employees.

subs.name: Nominations
subs.rule: Observations related to any nomination to the state government.

subs.name: Currency
subs.rule: Observations related to the minting of currency and civilian medals.
subs.see: 104 monetary policy.

subs.name: Government Procurement
subs.rule: Observations related to procurement processes and the oversight of contractors.
subs.see: 1610 military procurement; 1617 military contractor oversight.

subs.name: Government Property Management
subs.rule: Observations related to government property management, including the naming of public buildings.
subs.see: 2100s public lands management.

subs.name: Tax Administration
subs.rule: Observations related to tax administration
subs.see: 107 taxation; 1202 individual prosecutions for tax evasion; 2012 political activities of state employees.

subs.name: Executive Branch Scandal
subs.rule: Observations related to ethics or scandals involving the governor or other executive branch officials.

subs.name: Legislative Branch
subs.rule: Observations related to interbranch relations and legislative branch operations.

subs.name: Ethics, Campaign Finance
subs.rule: Observations related to the regulation of political campaigns, political advertising, lobbying, and government ethics.

subs.name: Census
subs.rule: Observations related to the Census.

subs.name: Capitol City Affairs
subs.rule: Observations related to Springfield as the Capitol.

subs.name: Claims Against U.S. Government
subs.rule: Observations related to the relief of claims against the Illinois government.

subs.name: State Holidays
subs.rule: Observations related to state holidays.

subs.name: Public Lands (General)
subs.rule: Observations combining multiple public lands subtopics, appropriations for public lands agencies, and general public lands policy.

subs.name: Parks and Recreation
subs.rule: Observations related to state parks, memorials, and recreation.
subs.see: 2103 commercial activity on public lands.

subs.name: Native American Affairs
subs.rule: Observations related to Native American affairs.
notes: This covers many subject areas that would normally be coded in other subtopics (housing, medical programs, transportation systems, etc.). See related coding guidelines above.

subs.name: Natural Resources and Forest Management
subs.rule: Observations related to the commercial use of public lands and public lands management.
subs.see: 709 animal and forest protection; 803 oil and gas leasing; 805 coal leasing; 1611 military land conveyances; 2101 land conveyance for national parks/monuments.

subs.name: Water Resources and Stormwater
subs.rule: Observations related to public water resources development, the Army Corps of Engineers and water rights.
subs.see: 701 drinking water safety; 711 water and soil conservation and watershed protection; 802 hydroelectricity; 1007 navigation and maritime issues.

subs.name: Territorial Issues
subs.rule: Observations related to U.S. dependencies, territories, and compacts of free association.
notes: This covers many subject areas that would normally be coded in other subtopics (housing, medical programs, transportation systems, etc.). See related coding guidelines above.
